summary: Full texts of both LactoSpore (B. coagulans MTCC 5856, 2 x 10^9 spores/day, 90 days) pilots confirm placebo-controlled primary benefits: GI symptoms in 36 IBS-D patients on standard care, and depression scales plus IBS quality of life in 40 patients with major depression and IBS (maker-sponsored). Both get eligible contexts limited to IBS/digestive outcomes, with depression not credited. A new applicability block limits credit to digestive outcomes.

applicability.studied_population: Adults with IBS (diarrhea-predominant on standard care, or IBS with major depression) taking LactoSpore B. coagulans MTCC 5856 2 x 10^9 spores/day for 90 days.

identity.standardization: Bacillus coagulans MTCC 5856 viable spore tablet

population.description: 36 newly diagnosed adults with diarrhea-predominant IBS at three Indian centres, 18 per arm, all on standard care (domperidone 30 mg, esomeprazole 40 mg, metronidazole 400 mg).

study_contexts.study_design: Randomized, double-blind, parallel, placebo-controlled multicentre pilot, 90 days, add-on to standard care; primary efficacy GI discomfort questionnaire symptoms (bloating, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, stool frequency).

dose.administration_frequency: one tablet daily at least 4 hours apart from standard care
dose.reported_regimen: [2000000000.0] CFU/day; 90 days; one tablet daily at least 4 hours apart from standard care

normalization.basis: Reported study-material daily dose, not a universal threshold or equivalence to other preparation.

source_provenance.location: Full text (PMC4769834): Methods (tablet formulation 2 billion spores supplied by Sabinsa, design, sample size, primary outcomes), Results Table 4 paragraph, Discussion (standard care), competing interests.

co_therapies: Standard care in both arms: domperidone 30 mg, esomeprazole 40 mg, metronidazole 400 mg; study tablet taken at least 4 hours apart.

outcomes.name: Primary GI-discomfort symptoms (bloating, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, stool frequency) decreased significantly versus placebo from baseline to day 90 (Table 4); VAS abdominal pain, Bristol stool and physician global scores also improved.

limitations: Small adjunct pilot, not monotherapy or other strain; multiple endpoints.
Exact strain Bacillus coagulans MTCC 5856 (LactoSpore), 2 x 10^9 spores/day tablets for 90 days; small pilots. Returned A008 date-only restriction withdrawn; assessed on verified full text.
Context authored and source-verified by agent review (Claude) on 2026-10-28; Dr. Pham's pre-approval of fully source-verified contexts attested by Sean on 2026-10-28.

population.description: 40 adults with major depressive disorder and IBS, newly diagnosed or untreated for 3 months, randomized 1:1 (20 per arm), multicentre.

study_contexts.study_design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicentre pilot, 90 days; primary outcomes HAM-D, MADRS, CES-D and IBS-QOL change (ANCOVA).

dose.administration_frequency: one tablet at least 30 minutes before morning meal
dose.reported_regimen: [2000000000.0] CFU/day; 90 days; one tablet at least 30 minutes before morning meal

normalization.basis: Reported study-material daily dose, not a universal threshold or equivalence to other preparation.

source_provenance.location: Full text (PMC6034030): Methods (600 mg tablets with 2 billion spores, eligibility, primary outcome), Results Table 3-4, Conflict of interest and funding.

co_therapies: Source-reported concurrent-care/restriction context: Agree not to use any medication (prescription and over the counter), including vitamins and minerals, during the course of this study.

Source-reported concurrent-care/restriction context: Subject’s assurance that they have not taken antibiotics or other supplements whose primary site of action is in the gastrointestinal tract for a period up to 1 month prior to the start of the study.

outcomes.name: Primary: HAM-D (day 90 5.9 vs 12.5), MADRS, CES-D and IBS-QOL improved versus placebo (p<0.01).
Secondary GI discomfort questionnaire, CGI-I/S and sleepiness improved versus placebo; serum myeloperoxidase fell (baseline imbalance 12.6 vs 9.8 ng/mL).

limitations: Small pilot, multiple outcomes; MPO baseline imbalance; not general MDD or other strains.

Authors are employees of Sabinsa/Sami Labs and the study was sponsored by Sabinsa. Credit for this record covers the IBS (digestive) outcomes only; depression results do not establish treatment of major depression.

freshness_search.query: ("MTCC 5856" OR LactoSpore OR "Bacillus coagulans" OR "Weizmannia coagulans") AND (irritable bowel OR gastrointestinal OR digestive OR bloating OR diarrhea OR constipation OR dyspepsia) AND (meta-analysis[pt] OR systematic review[pt] OR randomized controlled trial[pt])
freshness_search.screening_rule: Kept RCTs or syntheses of B. coagulans MTCC 5856 (LactoSpore) on digestive outcomes, and strain-level syntheses. Excluded other B. coagulans strains (GBI-30, Unique IS2, LBSC, BC99, SNZ 1969, BCP92), multi-strain products and animal studies.

read.title: The effects of Bacillus coagulans MTCC 5856 on functional gas and bloating in adults: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study.
read.finding: 2023 multicenter RCT: 70 adults with functional gas and bloating, LactoSpore 2 billion spores/day vs placebo for 4 weeks (66 completed). The primary GSRS-indigestion score (8.91 to 3.06 vs 9.42 to 8.43) and the global evaluation improved vs placebo (P<.001).

read.title: Outcome-Specific Efficacy of Different Probiotic Strains and Mixtures in Irritable Bowel Syndrome: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
read.finding: 2023 network MA, 81 RCTs, 9,253 adults with IBS: B. coagulans MTCC 5856 ranked among the most effective strains for abdominal pain (SUCRA 96.9%) and for IBS-D Bristol stool form (SUCRA 99.6%). Authors say confirmation is needed. Likely includes the credited trials.

read.title: Probiotic modulation of gut microbiota by Bacillus coagulans MTCC 5856 in healthy subjects: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-control study.
read.finding: 2023 RCT, 30 healthy adults, 28 days: safety and microbiome outcomes only; no clinical efficacy endpoint.

freshness_search.conclusion: confirms: newer exact-strain evidence (a 2023 RCT in functional gas/bloating and a 2023 strain-level network MA) agrees with the credited digestive outcomes, and no newer synthesis is null for them. Neither is added to the record's references; the credit still rests on 26922379 and 29997457.
